response.explanation: The hypothesis about ordering is not a defect. The first deleteMany only removes reminders whose scheduledDate has already passed, so their SendGrid sends have already gone out and cancelling them would do nothing. The defect is in the cancel query that follows. It filters only on cancelled=true and scheduledDate <= now+1h. It has no method: EMAIL filter and no check that referenceId is non-null. A cancelled SMS or WhatsApp reminder, whose referenceId is a Twilio SID, gets sent to SendGrid as batch_id. So does a cancelled email reminder that was never scheduled and has a null referenceId. SendGrid rejects the request and client.request throws. The single try/catch around the whole for loop then logs the error and abandons every remaining reminder. The reminder that failed is never deleted, so it fails again on every cron run, which keeps blocking the reminders after it in the list.
